title: Invocation Contract Gate: resilient schema sanitation, streaming resume & cross-sdk examples
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a lightweight 'Invocation Contract Gate' middleware for SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) that validates function/tool schemas at call-time, provides flexible coercion modes, and makes streaming invocations resumable and idempotent across retries. The gate should be pluggable in each language SDK and include canonical examples and tests. Goals: reduce runtime schema mismatch errors, provide predictable retry semantics for streaming calls, and offer cross-language consistent behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Middleware implemented for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs with unified behavior (strict, soft, coercive modes).
Round-trip tests demonstrating streaming resume using resume_token, and idempotent retry for partial responses.
Comprehensive example apps in each language under examples/tool-calls demonstrating function schema validations and retry scenarios.
Design doc and API reference pages in the SDK docs with usage patterns and migration guidance.
Performance overhead under 2ms p99 added latency for non-streaming calls; benchmark in CI.
tech_notes: Design: Gate sits between SDK caller and transport layer. On outgoing call, it performs: 1) Schema normalization: canonicalize parameter names, apply defaulting, run type coercion if in 'coercive' mode. 2) Signature validation: verify required fields, check enum constraints, and compute a deterministic contract fingerprint. 3) Attach metadata: include contract_fingerprint and optional resume_token in request headers/metadata. 4) On streaming responses, maintain a lightweight stream checkpoint that records last-ack sequence and resume token; integrate with existing stream-checkpoint API. Retry semantics: - Idempotent retries for streaming: if retry occurs, use resume_token to resume from last-acked token; if unavailable, fall back to 'replay' fallback policy which replays from beginning but deduplicates via request_id and server-provided idempotency hints. Modes: strict (reject mismatches), soft (log warning + attempt best-effort coercion), coercive (auto-coerce and normalize). Cross-SDK consistency: share JSON Schema artifacts stored in repo under /schemas and generate validators via codegen. Security: ensure contract_fingerprint is hashed (SHA-256) and avoid leaking parameter values in logs. Observability: emit metric sdk.contract_validation.{success,failure,coercion_applied} and stream.resume_attempts. Backward compatibility: default mode is soft to avoid breaking existing users.
implementation_plan: 1) Create canonical JSON Schema repo and generator (ENG-51781 dependency). 2) Implement Python middleware and unit tests. 3) Port to TypeScript, then to Go. 4) Add streaming checkpoint logic and CI tests. 5) Add examples, docs, and rollout as opt-in toggle via SDK config. 6) Canary rollout on hosted API with feature flag for 2 weeks, monitor errors and cost.
